Finding ways to track Starlink ‌users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals

Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users of Starlink’s ‌satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter.

Researchers at ​TrendAI, a unit of Tokyo-based cybersecurity company Trend Micro, concluded the Israeli company Discover-Tech was one of the biggest sources of digital ⁠ads shown to users of SpaceX’s Starlink service and that the ads were likely being used to geolocate or otherwise surveil them, according to the six people.

The researchers, who drew on digital advertising data in TrendAI’s telemetry for their conclusions, found that Discover-Tech had become one of the world’s leading bidders for ads aimed at Starlink ‌users and that it was the No. 1 bidder on Starlink traffic in more than 100 countries, including several where Starlink itself was banned or restricted. Bidding refers to the complex auction system by which advertisers secure space inside people’s browsers and apps.

SpaceX ‌did not respond to requests for comment. Discover-Tech and its chief executive did not respond to requests for comment over the past two ‌weeks.

TrendAI ⁠released a report on October 15 about the targeting of Starlink users but did not name Discover-Tech, instead saying the party ⁠responsible was “an ad tech entity” which it called “Shadow-Earth-79.” The six sources said Shadow-Earth-79 is TrendAI’s codename for Discover-Tech.

TrendAI did not directly address questions about why its report did not identify Shadow-Earth-79 by name, saying in a statement that its approach to attribution was aimed at reducing the risk of mistakes and avoiding “hype-driven labels” or “unstable actor names that can mislead defenders, distort ​risk prioritization, and trigger inappropriate response actions.”

Finding ways to track Starlink ‌users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals. Because they route data through SpaceX-operated satellites rather than nationally regulated telecommunications firms, the terminals can sidestep local internet restrictions, communicate in hostile areas or coordinate action across battlefields. Starlink has become a particularly important resource in Ukraine, whose military relies on the service for frontline communications and directing drone ‌strikes.

In May, Israeli newspaper Haaretz and the website Intelligence Online separately reported that Israeli-owned businesses were pitching clients on ways to identify and ​track Starlink users. Haaretz said exploiting ad data appeared to play a key role in the process.

The same day that TrendAI published its report on Shadow-Earth-79, Canadian cyber watchdog Citizen Lab and New York advertising technology ⁠firm Confiant outed Discover-Tech by name.

Both groups said the Israeli company abused the ad bidding process, which can leak data about internet users back to the bidder.

1. Core Context & Background: Finding ways to track Starlink ‌users has become a cottage industry as governments around the world try to get a grip on the spread of satellite internet terminals

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Experts at a digital defense firm recently found that an Israeli ad tech company was heavily targeting users of Starlink’s ‌satellite internet service in a likely effort to spy on them, according to six people familiar with the matter.

fullParagraphs: OpenAI in June unveiled its first custom AI chip designed with Broadcom, and said ‌it planned to deploy the processor by the end of this year

OpenAI plans to buy Google’s AI chips, ​ The Information reported on Tuesday, citing a person familiar with ‌the matter, as technology companies ramp up spending to ​meet surging demand for AI computing.

The ⁠reported plan would deepen ties between OpenAI and Alphabet’s Google, which compete in AI products and search but have increasingly struck ‌commercial deals. Last week, OpenAI said it would make its frontier AI models available through Google ‌Cloud.
The report did not disclose financial terms or ‌other details. ⁠Google did not immediately respond to a ⁠Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours, while OpenAI declined to comment.

Amazon, Microsoft and Google parent Alphabet plan to spend as much ​as $600 billion combined this year ‌on AI infrastructure as investors increasingly question when such spending will translate into meaningful returns.

Google’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) have gained traction as an alternative to Nvidia’s market-leading AI chips as companies seek cheaper ‌options. Google began selling TPUs directly to some customers this year.
Alphabet will report its quarterly results later on Wednesday, with investors looking for signs that its heavy investment in AI is continuing to drive growth in its cloud business.

Deals with customers including rival Anthropic have ‌fueled demand for Google’s TPUs. Alphabet expects to begin recognising a small ​percentage of revenue from TPU sales agreements by the end of this year, with the vast ⁠majority expected to be recognised in 2027, CFO Anat Ashkenazi ⁠previously said.

articles.title: India among top countries with highest heatwave exposure for infants, older adults: Report
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Globally, total number of heatwave days decreased from 2024’s historical high of 15.3 billion person-days for older adults and 2.3 billion person-days for infants

India ranked among the top countries with the highest heatwave exposure for both vulnerable age groups — infants and older adults — along with China, the U.S. and Russia, according to the tenth indicator report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change.

Globally, total number of heatwave days decreased from 2024's historical high of 15.3 billion person-days for older adults and 2.3 billion person-days for infants. The year 2025 was the second highest on record for heatwave exposure for both vulnerable groups combined as older adults were exposed to 10.8 billion person-days of heatwaves, while infants experienced 1.1 billion person-days, the report said.
When normalised by population size, older adults experienced on average 12.8 heatwave days per individual in 2025, while infants experienced on average 8.7 heatwave days per individual, it said.

Authors of the report, led by those at the U.K.'s University College London, said climate action is picking up around the world, but failing to keep pace with global warming, especially as health harms of climate change grew faster in the decade since the 2016 Paris Agreement, compared to the previous one.

A decade after the Paris Agreement, the report's authors are calling for climate change to be formally declared a global health emergency, for a new WHO instrument to enable a coordinated global response, and for governments to put health at the centre of every climate decision, from emissions targets to climate funding.

Priorities include urgent, fair cuts to greenhouse gas emissions, sustained investment in science, and climate finance for health delivered as grants rather than loans, so that countries can adapt without taking on more debt, they said.

"A decade after the Paris Agreement, our findings are unambiguous: the health harms of climate change are growing faster than the world's response to them, and in many cases even accelerating," author Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown, professor at University College London, said.
Real progress has been made in clean energy, health system readiness, and health-protective regulation, all of which are already delivering health benefits to local communities, Ms. Romanello said.

"However, progress has been too slow, too small, and isn't reaching those who need it most. That is why we are calling for climate change to be formally recognised as a global health emergency, with health placed at the centre of every climate decision," Ms. Romanello said.

articles.title: Are coronary stents necessary?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: There is a crucial distinction between stenting as a life-saving measure to medical treatment via stenting because a narrowing of blood vessels is seen on an angiogram

Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan’s recent remarks questioning “unnecessary” angioplasty procedures have drawn objections from medical organisations concerned that it could undermine public confidence in doctors. But the Chief Minister’s remarks demand more than a reflex response; it requires a thoughtful, honest response built on up-to-date evidence based on clinical and research studies.

Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI), by balloon angioplasty and stent placement, has transformed cardiovascular care. During an acute heart attack caused by a suddenly blocked coronary artery, prompt angioplasty and stents can restore blood flow, save heart muscle and improve survival. There is no debate about this approach and second opinions are unnecessary as time is of essence in such an emergency. Stents also offer substantial relief to selected patients with persistent activity-limiting angina (chest pain caused by lack of oxygen-rich blood).

There is a crucial distinction between stenting as a life-saving measure in the above situations to medical treatment via stenting because a narrowing of blood vessels is seen on an angiogram. A coronary angiogram shows the anatomy of the arteries; it does not, by itself, establish that a narrowing requires intervention. The decision to intervene and how to intervene must take account of the patient’s symptoms, the severity of the blockage, its effect on blood flow, the overall pattern of coronary disease and the expected benefit of intervention.
Kerala CM’s statement on angioplasty becomes a talking point among doctors
Public apprehension over unnecessary medical procedures should not delay treatment, say cardiologists in Keralam

The landmark ISCHEMIA trial , published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2020 , enrolled 5,179 patients at 320 sites in 37 countries with stable coronary artery disease and moderate to severe ischemia (restricted blood flow to the heart). The patients were assigned either to an initial invasive strategy — angiography followed by angioplasty or coronary bypass surgery — or to a conservative strategy of optimal medical treatment, with revascularisation reserved for those who had an acute event or angina. After a median follow-up of 3.2 years, there was no significant difference between the two groups in composite outcomes (cardiac arrests, hospitalisation for unstable angina or heart failure) and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality were similar. After a follow-up of 5 years, there was still no significant difference between the two groups in composite outcome or mortality. The core lesson is that most patients with stable coronary artery disease with ischemia on optimal medical treatment would do as well as those who undergo stenting or bypass surgery.

The growing scale of PCI in India deserves careful examination. National Interventional Council figures show that annual PCI procedures rose from approximately 1,13,000 in 2008 to more than 7,26,000 in 2024 — an increase of more than six-fold. In contrast, PCI procedures in the U.S. fell by about 40% between 2003 and 2016, reflecting progress in prevention and treatment.

These figures do not by themselves prove that stents are overused in India considering its large population, the substantial burden of premature coronary disease, the socio-economic progress in the past decades and the improved access to cardiac care centres. Nevertheless, the divergence in trends between the two countries raises an important question: how much of the increase in PCI is a reflection of fulfilling a genuine clinical need, and how much of it is a reflection of differences in practice patterns, financial incentives and gaps in knowledge on the efficacy of optimal medical treatment?

Optimal medical therapy, based on evidence-based guidelines, is the foundation of care for all coronary artery disease patients. The elements of optimal therapy include LDL-cholesterol lowering, appropriate anti-platelet treatment, blood-pressure control, evidence-based diabetes management and lifestyle changes. A coronary stent treats a specific narrowing; it does not cure the underlying disease of atherosclerosis or eliminate the risk of future heart attacks. Patients remain vulnerable to disease elsewhere in the coronary arteries and must continue preventive treatment.

The way forward is neither condemnation of cardiologists nor unquestioning acceptance of every recommendation for angioplasty. Most doctors strive to act in their patients’ best interests, but no profession is immune to inappropriate practice. The ultimate test of healthcare is not how many procedures are performed, but how many lives are saved and whether patients receive the right treatment at the right time at an affordable cost.

articles.title: ACB arrests Mirchowk inspector, home guard in ₹3 lakh bribe case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inspector demanded ₹6 lakh to close case against complainant’s father, ACB says

The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested Mirchowk Inspector of Police and a Home Guard on Tuesday for allegedly demanding ₹6 lakh and accepting a part payment of ₹3 lakh from a complainant in return for closing a case against his father.

According to the ACB, City Range-1 officials caught M. Kondal Rao on October 27 after he accepted the bribe through Home Guard Abid Ali. The ₹3 lakh in tainted currency was recovered from the possession of the home guard, the agency said.

The ACB said the alleged bribe was demanded in return for doing an official favour, including closing the case registered against the complainant’s father, avoiding coercive action, and providing future support.

The agency said the two police personnel had acted improperly and dishonestly to obtain an undue advantage. Both were arrested and are being produced before the Principal Special Judge for SPE and ACB cases at Nampally for judicial remand. The case is under investigation. The ACB has withheld the identity of the complainant for security reasons.
The agency urged people facing demands for bribes from public servants to contact its toll-free number, 1064, for action under the law.

articles.title: Days after claims of irregularities in garbage contracts, Chief Minister meets with legislators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday sought cooperation from MLAs and MLCs from Bengaluru to break what he called the “garbage mafia” in the city, even as the Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) is re-tendering 16 of 21 waste management packages.

Mr. Shivakumar held an all-party meeting at his official residence, Krishna, to discuss garbage management and development projects in the city. However, R. Ashok, Leader of the Opposition, who recently alleged irregularities in garbage management tenders, didn’t attend the meeting.

Mr. Ashok had accused the government of favouring an ineligible company and demanded a high-level probe into the matter. He said that one of the ₹133-crore tenders floated by the GBA had been awarded to a private company despite the firm failing to meet the eligibility criteria.

Meanwhile, Tuesday’s meeting saw discussion about the recent cancellation of tenders. Mr. Shivakumar briefed the meeting on the BSWML’s plan to restructure waste management by awarding 33 contracts for waste collection in 27 Assembly constituencies. The move is aimed at increasing the waste collection capacity in the city and ensuring seamless transportation, he said.

The new tenders would provide for the collection of up to 9,000 tonnes of waste. GPS tracking would be mandatory for all waste collection vehicles, and only new vehicles would be permitted under the contracts, he said. According to BSWML officials, only five contractors accepted the waste management tenders.

Karee Gowda, Chief Executive Officer, BSWML, told The Hindu that the rest have been demanding a nearly 30% premium on the actual contract value. The Cabinet had approved 14%, which was the discussion held during the meeting with stakeholders.
“The contracts are worth ₹584 crore annually, which the contractors want to scale up by another ₹180 crore. Thus, many refused to accept the Letter of Acceptance,” he said.
Meanwhile, the State government has invoked the Essential Services Maintenance Act (Esma) for waste management. Mr. Shivakumar sought the Opposition’s support “for the good of the city”.

Mr. Shivakumar reportedly said that they were working on changing the alignment of the North-South Tunnel, which had become a point of contention as citizens raised concerns over the possible impact on Lalbagh.
Meanwhile, he said the government had been working on a 10-year development plan for the city estimated to cost about ₹1 Lakh crore to mark 500 years of the city’s founding in 2037.

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday sought cooperation from MLAs and MLCs from Bengaluru to break what he called the “garbage mafia” in the city, even as the Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) is re-tendering 16 of 21 waste management packages.

Mr. Shivakumar held an all-party meeting at his official residence, Krishna, to discuss garbage management and development projects in the city. However, R. Ashok, Leader of the Opposition, who recently alleged irregularities in garbage management tenders, didn’t attend the meeting.

Mr. Ashok had accused the government of favouring an ineligible company and demanded a high-level probe into the matter. He said that one of the ₹133-crore tenders floated by the GBA had been awarded to a private company despite the firm failing to meet the eligibility criteria.

Meanwhile, Tuesday’s meeting saw discussion about the recent cancellation of tenders. Mr. Shivakumar briefed the meeting on the BSWML’s plan to restructure waste management by awarding 33 contracts for waste collection in 27 Assembly constituencies. The move is aimed at increasing the waste collection capacity in the city and ensuring seamless transportation, he said.

The new tenders would provide for the collection of up to 9,000 tonnes of waste. GPS tracking would be mandatory for all waste collection vehicles, and only new vehicles would be permitted under the contracts, he said. According to BSWML officials, only five contractors accepted the waste management tenders.

Karee Gowda, Chief Executive Officer, BSWML, told The Hindu that the rest have been demanding a nearly 30% premium on the actual contract value. The Cabinet had approved 14%, which was the discussion held during the meeting with stakeholders.

“The contracts are worth ₹584 crore annually, which the contractors want to scale up by another ₹180 crore. Thus, many refused to accept the Letter of Acceptance,” he said.

Meanwhile, the State government has invoked the Essential Services Maintenance Act (Esma) for waste management. Mr. Shivakumar sought the Opposition’s support “for the good of the city”.

Mr. Shivakumar reportedly said that they were working on changing the alignment of the North-South Tunnel, which had become a point of contention as citizens raised concerns over the possible impact on Lalbagh.

articles.title: City faces extreme groundwater depletion with abysmal levels recorded in Bachupally and Ameerpet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bachupally and Ameerpet in the city stand out among all mandals in Telangana in terms of groundwater extraction, by recording abysmal figures of Groundwater Drought Index (GWDI).
A large number of other areas in the city too are facing acute groundwater crisis four months ahead of summer, portending a bleak situation.

According to figures obtained from the Ground Water department, ‘Extreme Drought’ conditions with regard to groundwater depth are prevailing in at least fourteen mandals in the Core Urban Region (CURE) constituting the State capital. Five more mandals fall under the category of ‘Severe Drought’.
The Groundwater Drought index (GWDI) classifies the mandals based on the groundwater levels, into Normal, Mild Drought, Moderate Drought, Severe Drought and Extreme Drought.

GWDI is calculated by dividing the difference between historical mean depth to groundwater table below surface and the given month’s depth to ground water table, with the historical maximum depth to groundwater table for the same month. The historical figures are calculated based on the data from previous 10 years.
A GWDI greater than -0.15 is considered normal, -0.16 to -0.3 mild drought, -0.31 to -0.45 moderate drought, -0.46 to -0.6 severe drought, and less than -0.6 extreme drought.

Bachupally mandal in Medchal-Malkajgiri district has the worst situation in the State with a GWDI of -2.7, displaying extreme among the extreme drought conditions with regard to groundwater levels. Ameerpet is the next worst with a GWDI of -1.7.

Ameerpet also recorded the highest depth of groundwater in the State in the month of September, 2026, at 32.07 metres below ground level (m bgl). It is more than double the maximum depth in September at 13.36 metres, recorded in previous 10 years.

In Bachupally, it is relatively worse, as the depth in September, 2026 at 30 m bgl is more than three times higher than the maximum depth recorded for the same month over the past 10 years, at 9.06 m bgl.

articles.title: T.N. govt. revises housing loan limits for urban cooperative banks and credit societies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The maximum individual loan limit for UCCSs has been raised to ₹60 lakh for societies with deposits below ₹100 crore and ₹1 crore for those with deposits exceeding ₹100 crore

Cooperation Minister V. Gandhiraj has announced revised guidelines and loan limits for housing loans and mortgage loans offered by Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs) and Urban Cooperative Credit Societies (UCCSs).
The maximum individual loan limit for UCCSs has been raised to ₹60 lakh for societies with deposits below ₹100 crore and ₹1 crore for those with deposits exceeding ₹100 crore.
The maximum repayment period for housing and mortgage loans offered by both UCCSs and UCBs has also been extended to 20 years to reduce the monthly repayment burden on borrowers.

For UCBs, the maximum individual housing loan limit is ₹60 lakh for banks with deposits below ₹100 crore and ₹1.40 crore for those with deposits exceeding ₹100 crore, in accordance with Reserve Bank of India guidelines.

The Cooperation Department found that some UCBs had been offering loans below the limits prescribed by the RBI, leading to variations between banks. It has instructed them to extend loans up to the applicable limits.
The department has directed UCBs and UCCSs to review and amend their loan policies and by-laws and obtain approval from the Regional Deputy Registrar.
Eligible members can approach their respective banks or societies with identity proof, address proof, income certificates, and land or property documents to apply for the loans, the Minister said.

U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration has previously alleged that Flavio Bolsonaro’s father, former President ‌Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.

articles.title: Small fish: on Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.keyPoints:
• While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely
• Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.
• However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: River pollution from industrial effluents indicates state failure

The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

fullParagraphs: "Very severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” is continuing to interact with the land surface and the spiral band of the northern sector has further entered into the land," IMD said

The landfall process of the “very severe” cyclonic storm Arnab has commenced in Andhra Pradesh coast early on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) and the process is likely to continue for two more hours, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.

The system hit the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 125-135 kmph gusting to 150 kmph. The landfall process started at about 1.20 a.m. of October 28, they said.
Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab begins landfall near Narsapur, with heavy rains, wind, and surges threatening Andhra Pradesh coastal districts.
The centre of the severe cyclonic storm is very close to the coastline and the landfall process will commence during next 1-2 hours, said IMD in a post on X​ ​

With a severe cyclone expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Civil Aviation Ministry held a review meeting to assess the situation and ensure the safety of flight operations.

The ministry said flights to and from coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha, including Bhubaneswar, are expected to be most affected. Cyclone Arnab: Civil Aviation Ministry reviews situation to ensure safety of flight operations Civil Aviation Ministry reviews safety and flight operations as Cyclone Arnab threatens AP coast, with widespread flight disruptions and interagency coordination.
Civil Aviation Ministry reviews safety and flight operations as Cyclone Arnab threatens AP coast, with widespread flight disruptions and interagency coordination.

Heavy rain pounded the northern districts of Andhra Pradesh, leaving one dead and a trail of destruction, while southern Odisha remained on edge as the ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ Arnab moved closer to the coast.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm is likely to make landfall early — around 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28) – near the Yanam-Kakinada region in Andhra Pradesh. Initially, the IMD had said that the landfall would take place around forenoon on Wednesday.

Traffic on Ennore Expressway and other coastal roads in north Chennai and Tiruvallur district witnessed high waves lashing onto the land as a result of cyclone Arnab on Tuesday evening (October 27, 2026). Residents of Kasikoilkuppam, Ennore, Tiruvottiyur, Bharathi Nagar and Ramakrishna Nagar came out of their homes in panic, seeing the storm surge. Tiruvottiyur MLA N. Senthil Kumar, who visited the spot, said that there was no need for the public to panic. articles.title: Very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ begins landfall near Narsapur; Vizag battered by rain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: IMD experts said the landfall process may go on for a long time, and they can indicate the tentative landfall point only after the process is over
The very severe cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ has begun its landfall process near Narsapur town in West Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh, at around 1.30 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

Experts from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), however, said it is too early to indicate the exact location of the landfall. They said the landfall process may go on for a long time, and they can indicate the tentative landfall point only after the process is over.

According to the IMD, the wind intensity near the centre was reported to be 125-135 kmph, gusting up to 150 kmph. The wind intensity is likely to decrease after four hours. A high storm surge of 1.5 m to 2.5 m is expected over Kakinada and Yanam, the IMD said. Low-lying areas in these regions are facing the threat of inundation.

At Kakinada, which was initially indicated as the possible landfall point, the wind picked up speed around 1.30 a.m. However, there was no rain on the coast for more than two hours prior to the report of the winds.

The sea was very calm for more than an hour until the winds gained the strength to wreak havoc on the coast. The people had been waiting to witness how the cyclone would leave the Kakinada coast. In Uppada, stone boulders were spread on the road as the giant waves drifted them away from the shore line.

Those accommodated in the relief camps are keeping their fingers crossed about the damage to their houses and areas. In Uppada, a few thatched houses that are facing the sea have reportedly collapsed and their inhabitants are safe in the relief camps.
In Kakinada, several boats that were tied with the ropes to trees were washed away into the creek, leaving the fishermen to wake up only to see scattering of their boats.

In Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, scores of coconut trees have fallen along the roadside, and they are being removed by the NDRF personnel. No human loss has been reported in Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema and West Godavari districts.

Meanwhile, the northern parts of the State, especially the districts of Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, and Vizianagaram, continued to be battered by relentless rain. Between 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) and 1 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026), Kannuripalem of Anakapalli district received an extremely heavy rainfall of 231.5 mm, followed by 16th Police Battalion area in Visakhapatnam Rural mandal which recorded 223.91 mm, Chemalapalle of Pendurthi, again in Visakhapatnam district, recorded 220.04 mm. Parvada of Anakapalli district recorded 217.75 mm; Simhachalam area in Visakhapatnam district recorded 210.75 mm; and Atchutapuram in Anakapalli district recorded 206.75 mm.

In all, 12 stations from both Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli districts recorded extremely heavy rainfall of more than 200 mm from Tuesday morning (October 27, 2026) to 1 a.m. on Wednesday (October 28, 2026). Moreover, 188 stations in the districts of Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Anakapalli, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, Kakinada, and Parvathipuram Manyam recorded very heavy rainfall of more than 100 mm during this period.

articles.title: Former BJP MP Dharmendra Kashyap joins Samajwadi Party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: After joining SP, Dharmendra Kashyap alleged that the law and order situation in Uttar Pradesh has collapsed and that members of backward communities were being denied justice

Former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP from Aonla Lok Sabha constituency in Bareilly district, Dharmendra Kashyap, and his daughter, Kirti Kashyap, joined the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) in Lucknow.

Earlier, Mr. Kashyap resigned from the BJP and met SP president Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on October 11, accompanied by his daughter. Following the meeting, speculation about his joining the SP had intensified.

“The joining of former MP Shri Dharmendra Kashyap and his daughter, Ms. Kirti Kashyap, in the “PDA Movement” has multiplied our strength in Bareilly, Rohilkhand, and throughout Uttar Pradesh. We heartily congratulate them and all those who joined them. With our promise of ‘Respect for all, place for all’, we will move forward taking everyone along. Today is a special day in the sense that those who once fought elections face to face have today forgotten all competition and have united hand in hand for the larger objectives of the PDA,” said Mr. Yadav, while welcoming the former MP. Mr. Kashyap, hailing from the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category is influential in Bareilly district.

After joining the SP, Mr. Kashyap alleged that the law and order situation in Uttar Pradesh has collapsed and that members of backward communities were being denied justice. “Bulldozers are used against marginalised social groups under the BJP government. I assure that injustice will end and people will get justice in the future SP rule,” he said.
Uttar Pradesh / Bharatiya Janata Party / Samajwadi Party

articles.title: Bihar CM orders probe into legal notice served to RJD MP Sudhakar Singh by Kundan Krishnan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 15, Sudhakar Singh wrote to the Bihar CM about a defamation notice of ₹5 crore sent by Kundan Krishnan, asking whether the Bihar government endorse the notice

BIhar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) ordered probe over the issue raised by Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Sudhakar Singh with regard to defamation notice served to him by Kundan Krishnan, Director General of Police (Operation) and Special Task Force (STF) over Bharat Bhushan Tiwari police encounter case.

Mohammad Imran, Deputy Secretary at the Bihar CM Secretariat, has written a letter to the Home Department Principal Secretary for appropriate action to be taken on a letter received from Mr. Singh, concerning an impartial and independent investigation into the murder of Bharat Bhushan Tiwari, ensuring the accountability of the police command at the time, and addressing the legal notice for defamation served in connection with the raising of issues of public interest.

“As per instructions, it is requested that an inquiry be conducted or caused to be conducted. Please take an appropriate decision, inform the Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Sudhakar Singh, of the action taken, and provide a copy of the same to the Chief Minister’s Secretariat,”the letter stated.
Detained for six hours by Nawada Police, says RJD MP Sudhakar Singh

On June 17, 2026, Bharat Bhushan Tiwari, a young man from Bilauti village in Bhojpur district, was allegedly killed by the police in an encounter, and the incident created controversy. Later, Mr. Singh, an RJD MP from the neighbouring district of Buxar, raised questions over the “suspicious deaths” of Tiwari by the hands of policemen belonging to the STF.

On October 6, 2026, the police official sent a defamation notice of ₹5 crore to Mr. Singh for “false and disparaging statements” and sought a public apology within 15 days or face the ₹5 crore defamation suit.
On October 15, Mr. Singh wrote to the Bihar CM with regard to the defamation notice sent by Mr. Krishnan asking whether the Bihar government endorse the notice.

In the letter, Mr. Singh raised the point that according to the Central Government’s All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968, and the Bihar Government Servants’ Conduct Rules, 1976, any government official seeking to file a defamation suit in a matter related to their official duties must first obtain the government’s prior approval, in accordance with the prescribed provisions.

Addressing the CM, Mr. Singh wrote, “Could you please clarify whether this has been authorised by you, in your capacity as the State’s Home Minister, or by your government? Furthermore, if no such official authorisation has been obtained, I request that you ensure this gentleman receives training on government conduct rules.”

Mr. Singh further added that in the Bharat Bhushan Tiwari case, the CM and the Bihar government had acknowledged that the police committed an error and, on that basis, the concerned police personnel were suspended, an FIR was registered following a complaint by the deceased’s mother, and the government ordered a judicial inquiry.

articles.title: Bihar MLC results: BJP win one seat, counting underway on remaining seven
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As per initial reports from the counting centre, Janata Dal (United) candidate Neeraj Kumar is trailing in Patna graduate constituency which remained the hot seat due to boycott of Mokama MLA Anant Singh

National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) representing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Narendra Prasad Singh won the Tirhut teachers constituency seat by defeating independent candidate Bhushan Jha in Bihar Legislative Council polls.

Mr. Singh secured 2,945 votes, whereas Mr. Jha received 2,351 votes. Communist Party of India (CPI) candidate Sanjay Singh finished third with 1,967 votes. Polling for eight MLC seats in Bihar was held on October 23, 2026.
Counting is underway for seven remaining seats comprising four graduate constituencies (Kosi, Tirhut, Patna Darbhanga ) and three teachers’ constituency (Saran, Patna, Darbhanga).

As per initial reports from the counting centre, Janata Dal (United) candidate Neeraj Kumar is trailing in the Patna graduate constituency, which remained a hot seat due to the boycott by Mokama MLA Anant Singh. Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) candidate Dilip Patel is leading, whereas Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) candidate Anuj Singh for whom Anant Singh campaigned is in third position.
However, there is good news for JSP candidate Surendra Prasad Rai, who is leading in Darbhanga teachers’ constituency and sitting Congress MLC Madan Mohan Jha is trailing.

Similarly, Independent candidate Rahul Raj is leading in the Saran teacher constituency and N.K. Yadav of the BJP is leading in the Kosi graduate seat, followed by JSP candidate Rajnish Ranjan and Nitish Kumar of RJD in second and third position respectively.

In Patna teachers’ consistency, there was a tough contest between BJP candidate Nawal Kishore Yadav and RJD candidate Sajeev Kumar. In the Darbhanga graduate seat, RJD’s candidate Anil Jha is leading against BJP’s candidate Sarvesh Kumar.

Anant Singh who was expelled from the JD(U) for six years for anti-party activities, remained stuck to his claimed that Neeraj Kumar will face defeat. The final results are likely to be announced by Wednesday (October 28, 2026) morning as voting was done through ballot papers.

A 65-year-old man died at Mangalapalem after he came into contact with live electrical wires that had snapped and fallen into water. The districts of Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, and Srikakulam also recorded widespread rainfall of above 80 mm until 7 p.m. on Tuesday.

IMD, Amaravati, Director K. articles.title: Israeli exit polls indicate deadlock in election
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Polls closed at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT) in Israel’s pivotal general election, which saw high voter turnout and veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fighting for his political life

The first exit polls from Israel’s elections showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended Tuesday (October 27, 2026), but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The country’s main pollsters -- Channels 11, 12 and 13 -- projected the Opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats.

Israeli Arab parties also made gains after their voter base turned out in high numbers. The exit polls showed the two Arab-majority groupings, Raam and the Joint List, winning 17 or 18 seats between them.

In the last election, Likud walked away with 32 seats, enabling it to cobble together a coalition with smaller far-right parties after Mr. Netanyahu’s traditional allies baulked at the corruption cases the premier was facing.

This time around, those mainstream right-wing parties, by and large, vowed to work with main challenger Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party -- projected to nab 21 to 23 seats -- to form an Opposition coalition capable of unseating Netanyahu.
“The initial exit poll results indicate a complete lack of confidence in Netanyahu and the October 7 government,” Mr. Eisenkot said.
Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Mr. Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”.
While Raam and the Joint List do not belong to the Opposition bloc, they have expressed openness to supporting it.
Tuesday’s (October 27, 2026) poll was marked by high turnout, with many voters saying they saw it as pivotal for the country’s future.

articles.title: BRICS parliamentary forum expresses ‘deep concern’ about West Asian hostilities
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Joint declaration calls for a two-state solution to Israel-Palestinan conflict; asserts the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom, and an independent, sovereign state

Expressing ‘deep concern’ about the escalating tension and hostilities in West Asia, parliamentary leaders from the BRICS nations slammed “unilateral coercive measures” and “unilateral economic sanctions” imposed in the region as contrary to international law.

A joint declaration issued after deliberations led by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, at the end of the two-day 12 th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on Tuesday, also reiterated the need for a ‘two-state’ solution to the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

“We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia and, recalling our respective national positions, call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation,” the joint declaration said.

The meeting in New Delhi earlier drew attention as the Iranian parliamentary delegation’s chief, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, cancelled his India visit in the wake of growing hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi forces.

Despite the absence of Mr. Ghalibaf, who has been a key interlocutor in direct and indirect negotiations during the ongoing conflict, the forum provided opportunities for the exchange of views among stakeholders in West Asia. Several key policymakers from the region attended, including Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, Chairman of the Defence Affairs, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee of the United Arab Emirates.

Ties between the UAE and Iran have nosedived, as Iran attacked the Gulf nation as part of its strategy of retaliation against the U.S.-led attacks that began on February 28. Meeting a small group of journalists on the sidelines of the forum, Mr. Al Nuaimi spoke forcefully in favour of the two-state solution for the Israel-Palestinian crisis, without hurting Israel’s interests. “Around 160 countries recognise Israel, and it is a reality in the region. But the tragic situation has shown that the Palestinian state is needed. With this in mind, we need to restart the negotiation for a two-state solution,” Mr. Al Nuaimi said.

The joint declaration also addressed the ongoing conflict in the Gaza Strip. “We reaffirm our unwavering support for the peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the two-state solution, with the two States living side by side, in peace and security, in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, asserting the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom and an independent, sovereign state.”

The BRICS Parliamentary Forum obliquely addressed the U.S.-Israel attack on Iran and the BRICS stance against attacks on member countries, “We call for the elimination of such unlawful measures which undermine international law and the principles and purposes of the UN Charter,” the joint declaration said.

It condemned acts of terrorism as “criminal and unjustified” and condemned the April 22, 2025 terror strike in Kashmir’s Pahalgam in the “strongest terms”. It added: “We call for an expeditious finalisation and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism in the UN framework. We call for concerted actions against all UN designated terrorists and terrorist entities.”

The joint declaration added that inter-parliamentary exchanges among BRICS member countries provides a channel of communication and build trust among the member states. “Support the peaceful resolution of international disputes,” it said.

articles.title: India’s ‘balancing act’ risks eroding Russia’s trust
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: New Delhi’s performative diplomacy could undermine its longstanding friendship with Moscow

The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on August 31-September 1, 2026, and the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, were remarkable. Iran received considerably more attention and support from members of both the groups, far more than anticipated. More consequential, however, was the shift in India’s stance on the United States-Israel war against Iran and Russia’s war in Ukraine.

Traditionally, the SCO and BRICS summits have offered the three major powers — Russia, India and China — an opportunity to demonstrate their mutual solidarity. For Russia, it is a platform from which it can signal to the West that it is not isolated and still has powerful allies. The expansion of the SCO and BRICS under China’s leadership showcases its growing power to the West. For India, the SCO and BRICS have been useful for demonstrating its strategic autonomy. India has sought to remain welcome in both western and non-western forums, from the G-7 to the SCO and BRICS.

fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

Karnataka’s final electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been published, with constituency-wise lists of voters now available on the Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) website. More than 99.32 lakh names have been knocked off the rolls, as part of the exercise that was launched with the stated aim of ensuring that every eligible voter was included and every ineligible name removed to achieve a ‘pure, clean electorate’.

Political & National Report: Karnataka’s final electoral roll published after SIR. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary jurisdiction, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and statutory bodies responsible for upholding public accountability.

articles.title: EC appoints 11 nodal officers for 2027 Manipur Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Senior IPS officer Kamei Angam Romanus has been named the nodal officer-in-charge of the law and order and security plan, while IAS officer Hungyo Worshang will take charge of excise
Eleven nodal officers have been appointed by the Election Commission for the smooth conduct of the Manipur Assembly polls next year, officials said on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

Senior IPS officer Kamei Angam Romanus has been named the nodal officer-in-charge of the law and order and security plan, while IAS officer Hungyo Worshang will take charge of excise, a notification issued by the Manipur CEO said on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) evening.
Konsam Binku will look into election expenditure monitoring, and Khumanthem Diana will be the nodal officer for transport management, it said.
Nodal officers have also been appointed for computerisation, cyber security, communication plan, and other categories.
Assembly elections in Manipur are likely to be held in February-March next year.
Senior officials of the Election Commission had visited Imphal last week to assess poll preparedness across all 16 districts of the northeastern state.

articles.title: CTI writes to Rahul Gandhi again on INDIA bloc's November 1 rally, seeks meeting
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a letter to Mr. Gandhi, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted to explain how the proposed rally could disrupt business ahead of Deepavali

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) sought a 20-minute meeting with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to flag traders' concerns over business disruption due to the November 1 INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi and seek its postponement.

In a letter to Mr. Gandhi, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted to explain how the proposed rally, expected to draw 10 lakh people, could disrupt business during the festive season ahead of Deepavali.

This is the second time CTI has written to Mr. Gandhi in four days urging him to postpone the rally until after Deepavali. In its first letter to the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha on October 24, the CTI had said the postponement would help protect business activity during one of the busiest periods of the year.

In Wednesday's (October 28, 2026) letter, Mr. Goyal said, "We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders. So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy."

The traders would withdraw their protest if Mr. Gandhi convinced them that the rally would boost business and attract more customers. However, if they convince him that it would cause losses, then he should postpone the rally until after Deepavali, the CTI chief said.
The markets identified by CTI include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj, among others.
The other markets are Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market.
According to the CTI, the markets are located within a 1 to 5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan and could face business disruptions due to the rally.

In a letter to Mr. Gandhi, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted to explain how the proposed rally could disrupt business ahead of Deepavali

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) sought a 20-minute meeting with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to flag traders' concerns over business disruption due to the November 1 INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi and seek its postponement.

In a letter to Mr. Gandhi, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted to explain how the proposed rally, expected to draw 10 lakh people, could disrupt business during the festive season ahead of Deepavali.

This is the second time CTI has written to Mr. Gandhi in four days urging him to postpone the rally until after Deepavali. In its first letter to the Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha on October 24, the CTI had said the postponement would help protect business activity during one of the busiest periods of the year.

In Wednesday's (October 28, 2026) letter, Mr. Goyal said, "We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders. So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy."

The traders would withdraw their protest if Mr. Gandhi convinced them that the rally would boost business and attract more customers. However, if they convince him that it would cause losses, then he should postpone the rally until after Deepavali, the CTI chief said.

The markets identified by CTI include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj, among others.

The other markets are Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market.

According to the CTI, the markets are located within a 1 to 5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan and could face business disruptions due to the rally.

It crossed the coast between 2 a.m. and 8 a.m., about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40 km southwest of Yanam and 60 km southwest of Kakinada. They spent the entire night inside the godown until the police rescued them. All of them are safe and reunited with their families. They are natives of Yanam and Kakinada.

articles.title: No consistent improvement in Delhi’s winter air quality over four years: CREA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: There has been no consistent improvement in Delhi’s winter air quality over the past four years, despite the imposition of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), according to an analysis of government data by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), a Finland-based non-profit research organisation.

“Delhi’s winter AQI (Air Quality Index) has fluctuated over the past four years, with no consistent improvement. The mean AQI rose from 280 in winter 2022–23 to 304 in 2023–24, fell to 285 in 2024–25 and increased again to 295 in 2025–26. The median AQI followed a similar pattern, rising from 294 to 324, falling to 289 and then increasing to 305,” CREA said in a statement.

Delhi’s winter air quality has not followed a consistent downward trend since the 2022 revision of GRAP, and the mean and median AQI for the latest winter were both higher than in 2022–23, said Manoj Kumar, an analyst at CREA.

The mean and median of the AQI are statistical measures used to summarize air quality data over a specific period. Because AQI levels can fluctuate wildly due to weather changes or pollution spikes, these two metrics tell different stories about the air you breathe.

GRAP comprises short-term emergency measures to reduce air pollution and is divided into four stages, depending on the level of pollution recorded or forecast for the near future. The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) announces the different stages based on air quality forecasts.

Every winter, air pollution levels rise in Delhi-NCR and several parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains (IGP), mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and falling temperatures. Stubble burning during October and November, along with firecracker emissions, further worsens pollution.
Meanwhile, Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘poor’ category for the second consecutive day on Thursday.

The 24-hour average AQI stood at 223 (poor) at 4 p.m. on Thursday, down from 245 (poor) a day earlier, according to the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) daily bulletin, which provides the official AQI for the day.

The CAQM held separate review meetings with the governments of Punjab and Haryana in Chandigarh on Thursday to assess measures to prevent and control paddy stubble burning and reduce other major sources of air pollution. It directed the States to take prompt action on the ground.

The Commission emphasised the need to strengthen the crop-residue supply chain and ensure the effective utilisation of available machinery during the peak harvesting period. The meetings also covered field verification of burnt-area assessments based on satellite fire alerts, along with the district-wise deployment of drones and low-cost sensors to monitor stubble-burning incidents.

articles.title: Federal Reserve likely to skip rate hike despite elevated inflation
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation

The Federal Reserve is expected to stand pat on interest rates on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) even though inflation has accelerated in the past couple of months as the Iran war has caused spikes in oil and gas prices.

The Fed's latest policy meeting concludes less than a week before the midterm elections, which have focused heavily on concerns about the cost of living and affordability. Consumers have generally soured on an economy weighed down by more expensive gas, groceries, and clothing, among other items.

The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation. The Fed raised its key rate last month for the first time in three years, from about 3.6% to 3.9%, in what many investors and economists perceived was a first step toward a renewed effort to bring down inflation.

Yet Mr. Warsh faces a host of challenges in achieving that goal. President Donald Trump slammed the Fed for raising its key rate last month, though he largely blamed the central bank's rate-setting committee, rather than Mr. Warsh, whom he appointed. And some of the forces driving inflation — specifically the rapid build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure and higher energy prices — won't easily be tamed by higher interest rates.

At the same time, other parts of the economy are already being hit by higher rates, which were lifted by market forces, even before the Fed hiked last month. The average 30-year mortgage rate reached a three-year high of 7.4% earlier this month, though it has since slipped a bit. Higher mortgage rates have made buying a home unaffordable for 5 million more Americans since the beginning of the year, according to Oxford Economics, a consulting firm. Over time, Fed rate hikes can make mortgages, auto loans, and credit card borrowing more expensive, adding to Americans' sense that things like homes and cars are getting pricier.

After the Fed announces its rate decision, Mr. Warsh will speak at a news conference, where his remarks will be closely watched for hints about the Fed's next steps. He will likely repeat the Fed's desire for a “timelier” return of inflation to the 2% target. Some may view that as a sign the Fed will boost its key rate at its next meeting, in December, a move already widely expected by Wall Street investors.

If the Fed keeps rates on hold, Mr. Warsh will be pushed to explain why the central bank hiked rates in September but not this month. Inflation picked up in September, when consumer prices rose 3.7% compared with a year earlier. The increase was much bigger than the 2.4% rate in February, just before the Iran war.

And on a monthly basis, the consumer price index — the most widely-followed inflation gauge — rose 0.3% in both August and September. At that pace over a full year, inflation would rise much more quickly than the Fed's 2% target.

On Thursday (October 29, 2026), a separate inflation measure more closely followed by the Fed, the personal consumption expenditures price index, is forecast to have jumped 3.6% in September from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August. Core prices, which exclude the food and energy categories, are forecast to have risen 3.1%, up from 3% the previous month.

Aditya Bhave, head of U.S. economics at Bank of America, said economists and the Fed have gotten too complacent about above-target inflation. Higher oil and gas prices will likely keep inflation elevated for several more months, he said, and rising diesel costs will elevate shipping prices for nearly every type of good, which could spread inflation more broadly through the economy.

articles.title: Netanyahu and rival each claim mandate after tight Israel election
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Exit polls showed Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in Parliament

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot each vowed on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) to form a government after both came up short in the first election since the October 7, 2023 attack traumatised the country.

Voters turned out on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on the divisive rule of Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to the Hamas attack.

Exit polls showed Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu's hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in Parliament.

The strongest gains came from Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Mr. Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel.

Mr. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3 a.m. (0100 GMT), called for a "strong government of the right" and said that the "Jewish and Zionist majority must unite".
The 77-year-old Prime Minister was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory.
Instead, he listed leaders Israel has killed under his orders and again hinted that he was ready for a third bombing campaign against Iran alongside U.S. President Donald Trump, his close ally.
"Israel has a unique opportunity with our partner President Trump to forever eliminate the existential threat of Iran," Mr. Netanyahu said.
Mr. Eisenkot, speaking to his own supporters in Tel Aviv, issued a veiled warning to Mr. Netanyahu, who observers say could use a war to push for a unity government.
"Netanyahu, don't you dare use Israel's security for your political needs," Mr. Eisenkot said.

articles.title: Trump drastically loosens oil and gas methane rules
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran
U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) a sweeping rollback of rules that stop oil and gas producers from emitting methane, a greenhouse gas super pollutant.
Mr. Trump made the announcement at a rally in support of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who faces a tough battle for a U.S. Senate seat in November 3 midterm elections.
The regulations were put in place by Republican Trump's Democratic predecessor Joe Biden.
"Tonight, I'm officially terminating Biden's expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers $45 billion," Mr. Trump said at the rally in Lubbock, Texas.
To cheers from the crowd, Mr. Trump added that the move would "unlock vast quantities of Texas natural gas." Texas is by far the country's leading fossil-fuel-producing state.
An Environmental Protection Agency statement earlier this month gave the same $45 billion figure in cost savings, without offering a detailed breakdown of the savings.

"Americans must be able to afford to heat their homes in the winter and fill up their car and drive to work," said EPA administrator Lee Zeldin. "They can't do that when the people producing the energy are weighed down by unnecessary burdens."
Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran.
Polls show Republicans could lose control of Congress to the Democrats in next week's vote.

Methane, the main component of natural gas, is the second-largest cause of global warming behind carbon dioxide — responsible for about a third, or 0.5°C, of total planetary heating since the pre-industrial era.

articles.title: Two Britons charged in connection with assisting Iran over U.K. airbase incident
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: British-Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir, both aged 24 and from London, were charged under the National Security Act, U.K. prosecutors say
Two British nationals have been charged under the U.K.’s National Security Act in connection with an incident at the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford airbase on September 27, 2026.
Nouman Essghir, 24, and Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, 24, from London, were charged and scheduled to appear in court this week.

Mr. Abdulkarim was arrested for allegedly assisting a foreign intelligence service. The country was believed to be Iran , according to Laurence Taylor, the Head of the U.K.’s National Counterterrorism Policing unit.
Five men were arrested as they approached the air base in three vans on September 27. This resulted in the evacuation of residents in the air base area in Gloucestershire.
Essghir was initially released on bail before being re-arrested last week. Abdulkarim was arrested in the past week. Six other men have been arrested and released on bail as investigations continue.

British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the apparent plot was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard.
Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.
The suspects were subsequently released on police bail, which led to criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump.
An Iranian-British dual national was later arrested (and released on police bail) in early October.
Following the incident, the U.S. had removed its 12 B-1 Bombers , used in its strikes on Iran, from the airbase.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
